messages:
emma_customer: Hi — our July invoice shows ~720 reserved GPU hours for pool pool-78fa but the dashboard token usage is tiny. We only had a few bursts. Can someone explain why reserved hours were burned like this?

maria_support: Sorry about that, Emma. Can you confirm the date range on the invoice and the pool id (you included pool-78fa, correct)? Any example request ids that should be ignored? :eyes:

emma_customer: Yes pool-78fa, invoice period 2025-07-01 -> 2025-07-31. No special request ids; we mostly sent short embedding calls for a small subset of users.

raj_billing: Quick heads up on how billing works for Dedicated: reserved GPU hours are time-based (GPU uptime allocated to your reserved pool), independent of token counts. If a GPU instance is up/allocated to your reserved pool, it consumes reserved hours even if throughput is low. Burst usage is charged separately.

tyler_sre: Adding to that — typical causes: min_replicas/min_capacity kept nodes warm, node warmup settings, or autoscaler not scaling down fast enough due to cooldown/idle thresholds. Also some older configs pin a minimum of 1 full GPU, which results in ~24h/day consumption.

maria_support: Can you run this quick check for us?
```
# replace $TOKEN and dates
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" "https://internal.redwood.local/pools/pool-78fa/allocations?start=2025-07-01&end=2025-07-31" | jq '.'
```
This returns allocation intervals and replica counts; it helps correlate billing hours to uptime.

emma_customer: Ran it and attached a snippet — most days show 1 replica for 24h. I assumed replica=1 shouldn't bill full hours if idle; is there per-minute rounding?

raj_billing: We meter on allocated GPU time. Implementation notes: we report per-minute usage but invoices roll up and round to billing granularity (by default hourly buckets for reserved commitments). If you had 1 replica up for the whole day, that equals ~24 reserved hours/day.

tyler_sre: From allocation output I see min_replicas was set to 1 in the pool config and warm_pool_timeout was 3600s. That combination keeps at least one GPU up continuously. For non-prod workloads that want purely burstable behavior, set min_replicas=0 and lower warm_pool_timeout (e.g., 300s).

maria_support: TL;DR root cause looks like pool config + autoscaler cooldown: pool reserved GPU stayed allocated (1 replica) most of the month. Dashboard token counts are low but billing is for uptime.

emma_customer: Oof — that's our mistake in config. Is there anything you can do about the bill? We only intended to pay for bursts.

raj_billing: We can process a one-time billing adjustment for clearly misconfigured reserved pools if requested. To proceed we need: (1) your written request to support@redwood.ai authorizing a credit, (2) the pool id(s) and timeframe, (3) allocation telemetry we captured (we already have the allocation logs), and (4) agreement on the credit amount. I can provisionally estimate: billed 720h vs expected ~24h of actual bursts = ~696h credit. I'll open a billing case and include a draft credit note.

invoicing-bot: Billing case created #BILL-2025-782. Initial estimate: credit 696 GPU-hours. Pending manual review.

maria_support: We're happy to help with config remediation so this doesn't recur. Suggested immediate fixes: set min_replicas: 0 for this pool, set warm_pool_timeout: 300, enable aggressive scale-down (cooldown 120s). I can apply a temporary policy change if you want a hand.

tyler_sre: Also check any pinned model versions with 'pin_to_node: true' — those force allocation. And check if you enabled "guaranteed_capacity": true in the pool yaml. Example fix snippet: 
```
pool_config:
  min_replicas: 0
  warm_pool_timeout: 300
  scale_down_cooldown: 120
```

emma_customer: Please apply the changes, thanks. And please escalate the credit — this is a big unexpected cost.

raj_billing: Understood. I'll attach the allocation logs and a reconciliation summary to #BILL-2025-782 and route to finance for approval. Expected next steps: finance review (24–48h), then credit note issued on the next invoice cycle or as an immediate adjustment depending on approval.

maria_support: Applied min_replicas=0 + warm_pool_timeout=300 to pool-78fa just now (:white_check_mark:). Tyler — can you validate there are no pinned/guaranteed flags left?

tyler_sre: Confirmed — no pinned models, guaranteed_capacity was false. Autoscaler now scales down to 0 after idle. We'll monitor for 24h and report back.

emma_customer: Really appreciate the fast help. Please keep me posted on the credit status.

raj_billing: I'll update the case when finance approves. If you'd like an interim pro-rata refund instead of a credit note, specify in the support email and we'll evaluate.

maria_support: Follow-up action items: 1) Support to send email authorization for credit, 2) Billing will attach reconciliation (raj), 3) SRE will monitor autoscaling for 24h and post metrics.

emma_customer: Sending authorization now. Thanks all. :pray:
